extracted.intended_audience: Researchers/applicants preparing to resubmit NIH grant applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and policy requirements for resubmitting NIH grant applications (A1) following peer review, including timing, overlap, and administrative constraints. Covers what is allowed, prohibited, and recommended actions before resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact assigned program officer before resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: When you are ready to resubmit your application, you should contact your assigned program officer for guidance in addressing the comments in your summary statement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contacting the program officer is recommended to get guidance on how to address reviewers' comments contained in the summary statement prior to resubmitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult FAQs about resubmissions and differences
rubrics_metrics.description: See Frequently Asked Questions about resubmissions of applications for details about current NIH policy and to learn about the difference between a new application and a resubmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review the NIH FAQs to understand policy nuances (e.g., what constitutes a resubmission vs a new application) before preparing documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlapping applications may not be under review simultaneously
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not allowable to have overlapping applications under review at the same time. Two applications with overlapping aims may not be under review at the same time (Guide Notice NOT-OD-18-197).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prohibition applies regardless of activity code or Notice of Funding Opportunity (see related entry below). Check overlap of aims across all submissions before timing resubmission or new applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Only a single resubmission (A1) of an original application (A0) is accepted
rubrics_metrics.description: Only a single resubmission (A1 of an original application (A0)) will be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You may not submit multiple A1 resubmissions for the same original application; plan the A1 carefully to address reviewers' concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: A resubmission (A1) cannot be submitted before the summary statement is issued
rubrics_metrics.description: A resubmission (A1) application may not be submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous new application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You must wait for the summary statement from the prior review cycle before submitting the A1 that responds to it.

rubrics_metrics.name: A new application cannot be submitted before summary statement from prior overlapping application
rubrics_metrics.description: A new application may not be submitted before issuance of the summary statement from the review of the previous overlapping new or resubmission application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a previously submitted application (new or resubmission) has overlapping aims, you must wait for its summary statement before submitting a new application that would overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overlap prohibition applies across activity codes and funding opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Two applications with overlapping aims cannot be under review at the same time, even if they are for different activity codes (e.g., R01, R21) or if they are submitted to different Notices of Funding Opportunity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When planning submissions, consider all simultaneous submissions across activity codes and FOAs to avoid prohibited overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: No submission if substantial overlap with an application pending appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may not be submitted if it has substantial overlap with another application pending appeal of initial peer review (see NOT-OD-11-101).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an earlier application's initial peer review is under appeal and there is substantial overlap, you cannot submit the overlapping application until the appeal is resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission time limit: 37-month window
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH will not accept a resubmission application that is submitted later than 37 months after the submission of the new application that it follows (see NOT-OD-12-128 and NOT-OD-10-140).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure that any A1 resubmission is submitted within 37 months of the original A0 submission date, or it will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH statement on number of submissions with same content
rubrics_metrics.description: While NIH does not limit the number of times you can submit an application with essentially the same content and scope as an earlier application, overlapping-under-review rules and other timing/appeal constraints apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although repeated submissions with essentially the same content are not categorically limited by NIH, procedural constraints (single A1, overlap prohibitions, timing limits) restrict how and when such resubmissions can occur.
